memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He made the atonement cover of pure gold - two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide." - Exod 37:6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is the lid of the ark, and it is the theological centre of the entire tabernacle.

Inside the ark lay the tablets of the law — God's righteous commands, the very standard Israel had already broken. And directly over that law sat this cover of pure gold, where once a year the high priest sprinkled blood on the Day of Atonement (Lev 16:14).

Think about what that means. The broken law was not removed. It was covered. Between God's holy presence above and the accusing law below, there was blood.

That is the gospel in a single object. Our sin is not pretended away. The law still stands and still condemns. But atonement has been made, and mercy now sits over judgement.

Paul uses this exact image of Jesus: God presented Christ as a sacrifice of atonement, through the shedding of His blood (Rom 3:25). The word he uses is the same one the Greek Old Testament used for this cover. Jesus is where mercy meets the law.

If you carry guilt today, look here. God has not lowered His standard. He has covered your failure with the blood of His Son. That is why mercy triumphs over judgement (Jas 2:13).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you try to hide your sin, or bring it under Christ's covering?
2. What does it mean that God covered the law rather than cancelling it?
3. Is there guilt you are carrying that Christ has already atoned for?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, You are my atonement cover. Thank You that Your blood stands between me and everything that accuses me. Amen.
